abstract.para: Container technologies evolve rapidly upstream. To ensure &suselinux; 16 customers receive timely enhancements, security fixes and ecosystem compatibility while maintaining enterprise stability, container infrastructure components are managed under a dual lifecycle strategy combining an agile approach for standard components with a long-term stable model for core container engines.

section.title: Agile lifecycle model for container ecosystems
section.para: Most container components follow an agile lifecycle model, aligning closely with upstream project releases. This applies to general container infrastructure packages, including runcpackage>, docker, podman and their respective ecosystems, as well as helm.
Packages trail corresponding upstream project releases with an intentional buffer window reserved for enterprise hardening, security auditing and integration testing.

Updated versions are released across all supported &suselinux; 16 code streams, including versions under LTSS. If a new upstream major version introduces severe backward-incompatible changes, &suse; will diverge from continuous updates and defer the new version introduction to the next &suselinux; minor release.

section.title: Long-term stable Docker option (docker-stable)
section.para: For environments requiring extended release predictability without feature version bumps, &suse; provides a dedicated docker-stable package.

listitem.para: The docker-stable package is pinned at a specific major and minor release, maintaining the same version across all code streams.
From its date of release, docker-stable is supported and maintained for three years.
At the conclusion of the three-year support period, a new version of docker-stable is released.
